chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: Nat Nazarro looks for a Little Buck and Bubbles
summary: Nazarro comes looking for a young Buck and Bubbles; Green mentions Williams and Walker and Will Rogers teaching him to rope dance.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: But that didn't happen because Nat Nazarra came along, see. He was looking for a Little Buck'n Bubbles at that time. He already had the original Buck'n Bubbles. They were great stars. They were the biggest colored stars we had at that time besides like, see, because Bert Williams, he was the first one. That was Williams and Walker. They were very famous.
Had you met Williams and Walker up to this point?
No, sir, I never met them at all, see. I saw Mr. Williams once in Zigfield Follies with Will Rogers, see, and we became great friends before he died. Mr. Will
Rogers, he taught me to rope dance, and I still got the mark in my hand now from twirling the rope, you know.
He was a very nice man, you know. Everybody liked him too, see. And he used to come there, used to come to the studio, Billy Pierce Studio, you know. And --
